MITE_TYPE_WORD_2026-08-02.result: backlink+0xc reads 0x0125 for BOTH instances (0x80094cf4+0xc and 0x80094d10+0xc), while backlink+0x0 differs per instance (0x272a vs 0x2dec, clearly per-instance data). 0x0125's low byte is 0x25 = 37 decimal, matching the already-established 'type-word low byte == actor id' rule (Enemy_spawn_architecture.md/Archive) exactly -- the same rule already used to confirm id=40 (worm, 0x2528) and id=12 (grub, 0x060c).

AGGRO_2026-08-02.method: Landed one non-lethal hit on a live id=37 instance (movies/Phase4/Interpreter/mite_kill.json, the actor's own established fixture, hp 2->1 at f155 -- the same throw already characterized in COMBAT_AND_DEATH_2026-08-02) and tracked its own flags (+0x5c) and physical position (+0x04/08/0c) against Flik's stationary position for the following ~150 frames.
AGGRO_2026-08-02.result: The CHASE bit (flags+0x5c bit 0x2, the same bit already documented for Redbug and shell_bug) DOES set on the hit: 0x4011 -> 0x4013 at f155. But the actor's distance from Flik INCREASES steadily afterward -- 53424 units at f155, 54365 at f157, 58638 at f170, 65129 at f200 -- moving AWAY, not toward Flik. This is the SAME 'CHASE bit sets, produces no real pursuit' pattern already confirmed for shell_bug under D13, now independently reproduced for a second, unrelated species sharing the same underlying flag mechanism. Mite does NOT chase.
AGGRO_2026-08-02.closes: Closes 'mite-specific aggro/chase behavior' -- CONFIRMED NEGATIVE, mirroring shell_bug's own result.
